anchors.name: UNESCO guidance for generative AI in education
anchors.binding: Guidance from UNESCO for education and research.
anchors.asks: Notes that institutions are largely unprepared to validate generative AI tools. It calls for data privacy protection and a human-centred, age-appropriate approach to validating tools before staff and students rely on them.
anchors.evidence: A test of each AI tool on your own policy questions before staff use it, with wrong and missing answers counted.

anchors.name: EC–OECD AI Literacy Framework
anchors.binding: A common reference framework for AI literacy in primary and secondary education.
anchors.asks: 19 competences in four dimensions, written for teachers, school leaders, policymakers and learning designers.
anchors.evidence: A staff switch-on plan, with session records that name the framework's dimensions each session covers.

anchors.name: EU AI Act Annex III point 3: education
anchors.binding: Law in the EU: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
anchors.asks: AI used to admit or assign students, evaluate learning outcomes (including when they are used to steer learning), assess the level of education a person will receive, or monitor prohibited behaviour during tests is high-risk from 2 December 2027 (as amended in July 2026).
anchors.evidence: A description of each AI tool's purpose and users, for your legal team to classify.

anchors.name: UNESCO AI competency framework for teachers
anchors.asks: 15 competencies across five dimensions (human-centred mindset, ethics of AI, AI foundations and applications, AI pedagogy, and AI for professional learning), at three levels: acquire, deepen and create.
anchors.evidence: Switch-on session plans that name the competencies each session covers.
